mutant.description: ARM A's content-identity check is exercised on a live positive/negative pair from the SAME run rather than a synthetic mutant: committed-vs-worktree (identical content, EOL only) must read True, and committed-vs-served (genuinely different content) must read False. A comparator that returns a CONSTANT verdict regardless of input would fail the committed-vs-served case. Separately, the IAM census instrument (writer_census_ib_rtd_4.py) is exercised with two different actions (s3:PutObject, s3:GetObject) on the IDENTICAL key/ARN; a constant-returning simulator wrapper would return the same principal set for both, and it does not.
mutant.expected: committed==worktree (EOL-normalised): True; committed==served: False; s3:PutObject principal count != s3:GetObject principal count on the same key (both real IAM-policy-content-driven, not a fixed set)
mutant.observed: 'EOL-normalised: committed==worktree True; committed==served False' (both byte-level and, corroborating, PARSED-VALUE: True); writers (PutObject) 3 of 263 vs readers-by-grant (GetObject) 6 of 263 -- different principals returned for different actions on the same ARN, discriminating on real IAM content
